author: Vanessa Blasi
title: Frattolin pleads not guilty to killing daughter - NewsBreak
text: ELIZABETHTOWN, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — Luciano Frattolin pleaded not guilty to all charges on Wednesday in connection to the homicide of his nine-year-old daughter . Frattolin was arraigned in Essex County Court on an indictment charging him with second-degree murder and the concealment of a human corpse. Frattolin was taken into custody last week after his daughter Melina Frattolin was found dead in Ticonderoga on July 20. Officials confirmed after an autopsy was conducted that the child died by asphyxiation via drowning, and her death was ruled a homicide. Newly released indictment papers showed that Frattolin allegedly concealed Melina’s body in a pond in Ticonderoga. The indictment stated he allegedly placed her body “… in a wooded area in the water near a fallen tree with a rock on top of the corpse, with intent to prevent its production, use or discovery.” Essex County District Attorney Michael Langey and Assistant District Attorney Carrie Daly were in court Wednesday alongside Essex County Public Defender Emily Evatt. Langey argued that Frattolin should stay in custody. “He has no ties to our state, he has no ties to the U.S. I believe he is a flight risk,” said Langey. “He has an Italian and Ethiopian passport, I believe he’s dual citizenship there. He has an international drivers license for Ethiopia and Canada. He’s claimed residences in Canada as well as Ethiopia and has businesses listed in Canada as well as Ethiopia.” Langey also pointed out that Frattolin could have the financial ability to run from the law, if he were to be released on bail. “He has made it known that he had been in on a five million dollar property in Montreal at this time. He has shown that he has a $30 million bank account. He is, at least according to us, planned on or attempting to sell a mining company that has also been worth a significant amount of money,” said Langey. However, Evatt who represented Frattolin on Wednesday argued that he would have no reason to run. “If he is released, he intends to stay in an apartment in New York City with a friend whose name can be disclosed off the record for their safety,” said Evatt. He would give up his Italian passport which he has and be subject to electronic monitoring.” Judge Tatiana Coffinger ordered Frattolin to be held at the Essex County Jail without bail ahead of further proceedings. “I find that remand to the correctional facility is the only way to guarantee his attendance here in court because of the transient nature of the allegations, of his citizenship and really his ties to area. I can’t guarantee his return,” said Judge Coffinger. A compliance conference for the case is set for August 19 at 3 p.m., and hearings are slated to begin on November 12. Frattolin’s jury trial is scheduled for January 5 at 9:30 a.m. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to NewsNation.
